name: Trial
label: Equal Vision
lede: A Seattle straight edge band fronted by a professional juggler made one album, broke up the next year, and has toured more as a dead band than it ever did alive.

eras.title: The juggler takes the mic
eras.text: Seattle in the mid-'90s was a grunge town, and Trial was a political straight edge hardcore band in it. Singer Greg Bennick had been juggling for a living since his teens, and wrote about facing suffering rather than hiding from it.

years.h: Trial forms in Seattle around singer Greg Bennick
years.p: Greg Bennick and guitarist Timm McIntosh start Trial, a political straight edge hardcore band. Bennick took up juggling at 13 after being put in the wrong school minicourse; he'd picked coin collecting.
years.xp:
Bennick's way into hardcore was a friend's cassettes of New York radio shows, which he first thought were terrible. His first show was [[Hüsker Dü|5c4c90a4-539f-4101-83cf-301bc6a94e06]] in 1987, where he met Bob Mould and Grant Hart at a water fountain. For a [[Ramones|d6ed7887-a401-47a8-893c-34b967444d26]] show a month later, his mother forged him a birth certificate.

He never gave up the coins: Bennick is a numismatist who specializes in error coins and sits on the board of CONECA.

years.p: In 1995 a mysterious figure called Brian D. approached Trial about a record. Bennick told Razorcake that CrimethInc. was more a concept than an organization back then.
years.xp: Bennick told Punknews he watched CrimethInc.'s zine grow from one guy in an apartment. He also told Razorcake that band members and roadies were once arrested in Ohio on tour for shoplifting food.

years.p: Trial's second release, pressed as a 7" at 33 RPM and as a CD EP. It is later paired with Through the Darkest Days on one compilation LP.

years.h: Greg Bennick's forehead meets Timm McIntosh's headstock in Cleveland
years.p: Mid-set at a 1997 Trial show in Cleveland, Bennick's forehead hit McIntosh's guitar headstock at, as he put it to Punknews, about a trillion miles per hour. He bled badly.
years.xp: Another road story Bennick told Punknews: his Orthodox Jewish cousin came to her first hardcore show when Trial played Philadelphia. While he was showing her the van, a member of another band on the bill, who had offended [[Floorpunch|8ecf80c2-d090-4cbd-97ec-0a0824301041]], dove inside and locked the doors. Floorpunch members in varsity jackets pounded on the windows until the man slipped away into the night.

eras.title: Months staring at walls
eras.text: Three members quit while Trial was writing its only album, leaving Bennick and McIntosh to finish it with borrowed help. Equal Vision put it out, and a year later the band was done, fighting over the future and unhappy with the label.

years.h: Trial rebuilt: Alexei Rodriguez learns the album in three days
years.p: Three original members quit while Are These Our Lives? was being written. Bassist Brian Redman came in, and drummer Alexei Rodriguez, borrowed from Catharsis, learned the album in three days and tracked it in a day and a half.

q: Still totally happy with it musically and lyrically.
years.h: Are These Our Lives? comes out on Equal Vision
years.p: Trial's only full-length. Greg Bennick spent months on the lyrics, but Equal Vision's first pressing ran without them in the insert.
years.xp:
Bennick told Punknews he'd spent months staring at walls, thinking of words, and that the label was more excited about radio than the record's message. The only thing he'd change is one phrase in One Step Away.

Trial now treats Panic Records' reissues, with the full lyrics and new liner notes, as the authorized versions, and Bennick says Equal Vision isn't authorized to reissue it.

years.h: Trial break up, fighting over the stupidest things
years.p: A year after Are These Our Lives?, Trial split. Greg Bennick told Razorcake the band had become a dysfunctional relationship on the verge of explosion, and told Punknews the label's handling of the album was part of it.

eras.title: A post-mortem existence
eras.text: Bennick turned his fixation on death into a documentary while Trial came back a few shows at a time. In 2009, weeks after the band's best summer, its bassist was killed.

years.p: Bennick co-produced Flight from Death with Patrick Shen, a film on how the fear of death drives human violence. Narrated by Gabriel Byrne, it won audience choice for best documentary at the Beverly Hills Film Festival.

years.h: Trial reunite for Seattle, London and Budapest
years.p: Trial play three reunion shows in Seattle, London and Budapest. A compilation pairing Through the Darkest Days and Foundation comes out the same year.

years.h: Trial play the Burning Fight book release in Chicago
years.p: Trial play the release show for Burning Fight, Brian Peterson's book on '90s hardcore, in Chicago.

years.h: Trial headline Fluff Fest in the Czech Republic
years.p: Trial headline Fluff Fest on July 25, 2009, then play Antifest in Stockholm in August.

years.src: Exclaim! · DIY Conspiracy (2009) · Wikipedia: Trial (Seattle band)
years.h: Trial bassist Brian Redman dies in a scooter crash
years.p: Brian Redman, who played on Are These Our Lives? and later in 3 Inches of Blood, died at 31 in a scooter crash in Tacoma, Washington, Exclaim! reported.
years.xp:
Exclaim!, citing police, reported that he was thrown from the scooter after apparently striking a curb. Trial's statement called him one of the most sincere, sarcastic, witty, intelligent, talented guys.

Greg Bennick told DIY Conspiracy a few weeks later that hundreds of people had written to him, and that the band was on hold.

eras.title: More shows than the first time
eras.text: After two quiet years Trial came back harder than ever, with European tours and runs through North America, shows Bennick called celebrations in Redman's memory rather than reunions. The last one was in 2018.

years.h: Trial return: Rainfest, The Rumble, Tsunami Fest, Sound and Fury
years.p: After two years off, Trial play Seattle's Rainfest, Chicago's The Rumble, East Coast Tsunami Fest, a surprise New York show and Sound and Fury in Santa Barbara.
Trial tour Europe for thirty shows, more than they ever managed in the '90s. Greg Bennick told Razorcake the post-2009 shows were celebrations honoring Brian Redman, not reunions.

years.big: A dead band that tours more than ever
q: I have to wonder what it means to be a 'real band'.
years.h: Trial play 15 North American shows in two weeks
years.p: Twelve years after breaking up, Trial tour North America, with Jason Shrout drumming on the West Coast. Greg Bennick is also singing in [[Between Earth & Sky|eb394966-a942-4480-a896-9ecd2fd2847e]].

years.h: Trial tour Europe with By the Grace of God
years.p: Trial go back to Europe alongside Louisville's [[By the Grace of God|42a5a24f-7fa9-4790-879d-fe5fb3d91f9f]], according to Discogs.

years.h: Trial's last show: New Age Records' 30th anniversary
years.p: Trial play New Age Records' 30th anniversary festival at the Garden Amphitheater in Garden Grove, California, with [[Strife|5e911223-4228-4a14-8f6c-7d2dfeb62530]] and [[Mouthpiece|e4a55353-84ff-4460-9d5a-1666fbe104f4]]. Discogs lists it as the band's final performance.

years.h: Greg Bennick's next band, Bystander, asks Where Did We Go Wrong?
years.p: Bennick's post-Trial straight edge band Bystander releases the EP Where Did We Go Wrong?, featured on No Echo.
